title: Cars, Trains or Planes: How Do Europeans Travel?
paragraphs: How do people in the EU mostly get around — by car, train, bus or plane?
According to new Eurostat data, cars are still by far the most common choice. But the way people travel is slowly changing, and for the first time in a decade, trains have overtaken buses.
The data was published by the EU's statistical office in September 2026 and is based on travel in 2024.

Cars made up around 69% of passenger travel across the EU, followed by planes at around 16%. Trains were next, at 7.5%, while buses — including long-distance buses and trackless trolleys — were just behind at 7.3%.
It was the first time since 2014 that trains had a larger share than buses.
But even though cars still lead, their share has fallen by 2.9 percentage points since 2014.
Air travel, however, saw the biggest growth over the decade, going up by 3.6 percentage points. Train travel also grew, but by a smaller 0.9 points, while buses fell by 1.3 points.
Of course, how people get around depends a lot on where they live.
Lithuanians used cars the most, with around 84% of passenger travel done by car. The Netherlands and Finland came next.
Croatia had the highest share of air travel, at about 46%. Its many islands and strong tourism industry may help explain why flying is so important there.
Trains were most popular in Hungary and Austria, while buses were used the most in Malta and Ireland.
Malta has no rail network at all, while in Ireland buses reach many places that trains do not.
